finding: Utah's hierarchy is documented by Utah: boundary → hunt → season, keyed by hunt_number. What is missing is the CODE BOOK, not the model.

correctsMyEarlierFinding.whatIsaid: “Not a licence, not an endpoint, and not a key: a model of which boundary applies to which species and hunt type, which Utah encodes in the hunt tables beside this layer rather than in the geometry.”
correctsMyEarlierFinding.whatIsMeasuredNow: The model is IN the service and the authority documents it in its own words. Layer 0's description reads: “DWR_Combined_Hunt_Boundaries - Holds each unique hunt boundary. DWR_Hunt_Boundary_Info - Many hunts can occur on each boundary (hunt_number is the key) DWR_Hunt_Boundary_Season - Many date ranges can occur for each hunt (hunt_number is the key)”. Table 1, NRDWRGIS.%HUNT_INFO_MOBILE, carries 3,037 rows of BOUNDARY_NAME, SEASON, BOUNDARYID and HUNT_NUMBER.
correctsMyEarlierFinding.soTheObstacleMoves: From ‘no model exists here’ to ‘the model exists and nothing in the service decodes its keys’, which is a different and more tractable problem.

theHierarchy.shape: boundary (unique geometry) ← many hunts (hunt_number is the key) ← many date ranges
theHierarchy.whyAPointIN25BOUNDARIESISCORRECT: A Utah point falling inside 25 Active boundaries is not a defect in the data or in our resolver. Utah's geography does not narrow to one answer: WHICH HUNT a person is on selects the boundary, not the other way round. Every other state in the corpus resolves point → unit → rules; Utah resolves point → SET of boundaries, and the hunt chooses among them. That is the hierarchy primitive, and it needs the hunt as an input rather than a better polygon.
theHierarchy.huntNumberIsStructured: A coded key, not prose: 1,000 distinct values returned before the service's transfer limit, across 29 letter prefixes.

theCodeBookIsNotPUBLISHED.measured: No field domain on any column of table 1; no table description; no copyrightText; no relationships declared on layer 0. Nothing in the service maps a prefix to a species, a legal animal class or an implement.
theCodeBookIsNotPUBLISHED.whyItIsNotGUESSED: DB, EA, EB, BR, EL, CG, PB, MB, BI and TK all suggest readings, and §8 forbids exactly that: never infer a legal fact from shorthand. A wrong decode would attach one species' season to another species' ground and look entirely normal.
theCodeBookIsNotPUBLISHED.whereItProbablyIS: Utah's own guidebooks. The SEASON text points at them itself — one value reads “Any open season on any open bear unit during the 2026 season. See 2026 Black Bear Guidebook for season dates and take methods.”
theCodeBookIsNotPUBLISHED.whatWouldSettleIt: A published mapping from hunt-number prefix to species and hunt type, from DWR's own guidebooks or tables.

seasonIsADISPLAYSTRING.finding:
SEASON is not structured data. 252 distinct values, several carrying HTML markup — “Ducks, Mergansers, Coot & Snipe: Oct 10, 2026 - Jan 23, 2027
Scaup: …” — and several differing from each other only by trailing whitespace.
seasonIsADISPLAYSTRING.consequence: §8 applies directly: a fact that lives only in a display string is not resolved. Utah's dates would have to be parsed out of mobile-app prose, which is an extraction task with its own error surface, not a read.

instrumentFailuresWorthKnowing: resultOffset is REJECTED by this server: `&resultOffset=0` returns HTTP 400 ‘Failed to execute query’, so the table cannot be paged that way and 1,000 rows is the ceiling of one request.
returnDistinctValues combined with returnCountOnly also returns HTTP 400, so the true distinct count of HUNT_NUMBER is not established — only that it is at least 1,000.

A query adding BOUNDARY_NAME (a 600-character column) with resultRecordCount=4000 returned HTTP 400 while the same query without them succeeded. Three different 400s from one server, none of them a refusal of access: this is the same shape as the earlier Utah measurement whose malformed Status clause returned zero boundaries and nearly became ‘Utah does not cover its own towns’.
unchanged: Utah is still NOT_SERVABLE_AS_A_ZONE_LAYER and no Utah rule is certified. Nothing here is encoded as a rule or a zone.
